extracted.intended_audience: patent chemical indexers, database searchers, and abstractors who assign/search Derwent chemical codes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for assigning and searching Derwent chemical element and functional-group codes in patent documents, including how to treat metals, ions/ligands, Part A/B/C code selection, and special-case conventions (dates, tautomers, mixtures vs complexes).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-character element symbol shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: One-character element symbols (e.g., T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z) are used as a chemical shorthand for groups of atoms that are coded similarly; these symbols remain consistent throughout the manual but some chapters define additional element symbols or variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the notes in each chapter to determine chapter-specific meanings. The manual provides mappings (e.g., T = O, S, Se, Te; U = O, S, Se, Te or N; V = heteroatom other than O,S,Se,Te,N; W = O,S,Se,Te,N,C or halogen in Parts H: through L:, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'additionally coded' / 'also coded'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrases 'additionally coded' and 'also coded' indicate that two different code Sets or Subsets are used: the one where the phrase appears and the one to which the user is referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such phrasing appears, apply both the local code and follow the cross-reference to apply the second code set as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'as applicable' / 'if applicable'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrases 'as applicable' and 'if applicable' mean the referred-to codes can potentially be used, but their definitions and rules must be consulted to determine whether they actually fit the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume applicability; verify definitions and rules before assigning the cross-referenced codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation separates equally applicable code definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The punctuation marks ';' and ',' are used to separate equally applicable code definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'P448 Tranquiliser; anxiolytic' means P448 is equally applicable to a tranquiliser, an anxiolytic, or a compound that is both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-anchor 'From 1981 forward' semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: References like 'From 1981 forward' mean 'From 1981/Derwent Week 27 forward'—1981/week-27 is the manual's date anchor for code applicability changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'From 1981 forward' specifically as 'From 1981/Derwent Week 27 forward' when deciding code validity by date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Other' in code definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'other' in a code definition covers all relevant, specific possibilities other than those already defined by immediately preceding codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes should be read in the order listed; earlier codes exclude their categories from 'other'. Example: V500..V570 list specific microorganisms; V570 = 'Other specific microorganism' for those not covered by earlier codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which compounds Parts A:, B:, C: cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts A:, B:, and C: are used to identify/describe individual elements present in specific types of compounds: inorganic compounds; inorganic ions and ligands bonded to organic/inorganic groups; organic compounds containing P, As, B, Si, Se, Te; organometallic compounds; and free elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most other organic compounds are not usually assigned Part A/B/C codes and should be coded via rings, functional groups, and carbon chains (Parts H:–L:), except special cases noted in Part C: notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valency definition for coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Valency of an atom is defined as the number of bonds in which it participates; double bonds count as two, coordination bonds count as two, and triple bonds count as three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this bond-counting rule when assigning valency-related codes (e.g., B80: valency codes). Example diagrams in the manual illustrate non-standard valencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide compounds into ions/ligands for coding
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting codes for an ionic or coordinated compound, divide the compound into its component ions or ligands and consider each separately for code selection, even if codes are overcoded in a single subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search ions/ligands as if only one formula unit of each is present; this affects counts of elements, functional groups, and rings. See coding examples illustrating this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements Absent codes (C80:) apply collectively to inorganic ions/ligands
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive one or more Elements Absent codes from Subset C80:, the element(s) must be absent from all inorganic ions or ligands in the compound (i.e., apply collectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negation codes in Parts H:–L:, carbon chain codes M280/M320, and Basic Group codes M41/M42 also apply collectively to all organic ions and ligands of the compound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding inorganic ions/ligands bonded to organic groups only when important
rubrics_metrics.description: Inorganic ions and ligands bonded to organic groups are usually coded only when they are important to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical note: prior to 1981 some metal salts of organic acids were coded differently; since 1963 all metal salts of organic acids have been assigned A960 and C710. Alkali and alkaline earth metals are only coded when limiting/important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy for complexes vs mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: For comprehensive retrieval of complexes, perform two searches: (1) search the complex as a single compound, and (2) search the component compounds as if they are a simple mixture; combine the component searches with AND and then OR the result with the complex search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AND (not LINK) to combine component codes because component codes may be listed in separate subfields; OR the ANDed result with the single-compound search to retrieve both types of patents (mixtures and true complexes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part A: code numeric structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Part A: codes have first digit indicating the metal group and last two digits (up to 99) indicating the atomic number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this structure to interpret and to construct truncated searches (e.g., truncating after second character 'A4:' retrieves all First Transition Series metals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic Part A: codes ('00') are not sufficient alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic Part A: codes ending in '00' are assigned for generic group disclosures but are not sufficient alone to retrieve all references to metals within that group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To retrieve all references to a group, OR the codes for all individual metals with the generic '00' code, or search the truncated Set code (e.g., 'A4:').

rubrics_metrics.name: Part C: descriptors supplement Part A:
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional descriptors for compounds receiving Part A: codes are found in Part C: (e.g., C710 identifies inorganic cation in an organic compound).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Part C: notes for use of additional descriptors when coding metal-containing compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: delete non-C bonds to metal when dividing compound
rubrics_metrics.description: When coding metal-containing compounds, first divide the compound into component ions or ligands; delete all bonds to the metal atom(s) except those from organic carbon atoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first step in the metal-coding algorithm; a following step assigns Part A: codes to each metal (except As, which is in Part B:).

rubrics_metrics.name: Each metal receives Part A: code (except arsenic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each metal in the compound receives the Part A: code that identifies it; arsenic is coded in Part B: instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note there are no 'Poly' codes in Part A: to indicate multiple formula units of a metal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use A91:, A92:, A930 to describe metal–C bonding patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use codes in Subsets A91: and A92: and the code A930 to describe various types of bonds between metal atoms and organic carbon atoms (e.g., A910 = one bond to C; A922 = metal bonded to two C atoms in same ring; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structures coded A930 are additionally coded A910 or in Subset A92: depending on number/type of C–metal bonds; organometallic fragments receive applicable H:–L: codes as well (e.g., -C(=W)- fragment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metal bonded to non-organic-C assumed ionic/coordinate; assign A940–A980
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond between a metal atom and an atom other than organic carbon is assumed to be ionic or coordinate, and the group bonded to the metal is considered a separate ion or ligand for coding purposes; assign one of A940 (metal bonded to inorganic anion), A950 (metal bonded to inorganic neutral ligand), A960 (metal bonded to O,S,Se,Te,N of an organic group), A970 (metal bonded to an organic ion/ligand excluding earlier cases), or A980 (metal is member of an inorganic anion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If metal is bonded to B, Si, P, or As, also search B770 in addition to applicable A94:/A95: codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metal carbides coded organic only if C bonded to H
rubrics_metrics.description: Metal carbides are considered organic for coding purposes only when the carbon is bonded to one or more hydrogen atoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise treat metal carbides per inorganic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding ions/ligands bonded to metal: replace metal with protons for ions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ions or ligands bonded to metal atoms are coded individually in the code Parts that apply to them, with protons replacing metal atom(s) in the case of ions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applicable codes for metal and ions/ligands are overcoded in a single code subfield; however, two or more complex organic fragments in a single compound may be coded in separate subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to search functional groups bonded to metal via carbon
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional groups in organic ions/ligands bonded to a metal atom via carbon are searched in Parts H:–L: in one of two ways: as if the metal were replaced by H when the metal is bonded to only one carbon atom, or as if the metal were replaced by carbon when the metal is bonded to more than one carbon atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the replacement rule to determine which H:–L: functional-group codes are applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautomer coding preference: favour heteroatom tautomer
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compound can exist as either a metal–C or a metal–heteroatom tautomer, only the metal–heteroatom tautomer is coded; the metal–tautomer bond is assigned the appropriate A94:–A98: code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer coding the heteroatom tautomer and apply A940–A980 as the bond descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: A9: bonds to metal atoms - code definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subheadings A9 and its codes describe metal–carbon bonding patterns: A910 = one bond from metal to organic C; A921/A922/A923 = distinctions for two or more C bonds (e.g., A922 = metal bonded to two C atoms in same ring); A930 indicates metal–W (= any heteroatom) fragments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structures coded A930 are additionally coded A910 or A92: depending on the case; the -C(=W)- fragment also receives applicable H:–L: codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: A940–A980: metal–ligand/anion/neutral ligand code meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific A94:/A95:/A96:/A97:/A98: codes identify the nature of the non-C ligand/anion: A940 = metal bonded to an inorganic anion; A950 = metal bonded to an inorganic neutral ligand (e.g., CO, NO, PH3, NH3); A960 = metal bonded to O, S, Se, Te, or N of an organic ion/ligand; A970 = metal bonded to an organic ion/ligand excluding earlier subsets; A980 = metal is member of an inorganic anion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: A950 and others have date applicability (1970); when metal bonds to B, Si, P, or As, include B770 additionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B: which elements and contexts it covers
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B: covers noble gases, boron, silicon, phosphorus, arsenic, selenium, and tellurium (collectively 'Part B: elements' or 'Z atoms'), both as free elements and in compounds, ions, and ligands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B: codes indicate the element and the type of compound context (free element, inorganic compound, inorganic anion/cation of an organic compound, aliphatic, carbocyclic, heterocyclic, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority order for Part B: code selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one Part B: code is used to identify a Part B: element; the code is chosen according to the priority order: B1 = B2 = B3 > B6 > B5 > B4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a P atom in a heterocyclic compound receives B615 but not B515 or B415; follow the specified priority when multiple contexts could apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B: numeric code structure and noble gases
rubrics_metrics.description: The last two digits of codes in Sets B0: through B6: correspond to the atomic number; codes ending in '00' are used in Sets B1:–B6: to indicate noble gases (generic noble gas codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use atomic-number decoding to identify specific element codes; consult date applicability for noble-gas codes (e.g., B000 used before 1981).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding Se/Te: include replacement-S rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds with Se or Te receive the applicable Se or Te element code from Part B:, plus any codes from Parts A: through L: that would apply to the compound if the Se/Te atoms were replaced by sulfur, with exceptions (codes in Set C5: and code C801 are not assigned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply S-based codes as well unless explicitly excluded; consult Part C exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for functional groups bonded to Z atoms (Subset B79:)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Subset B79: are assigned to every structural fragment matching their code definitions; in many cases these B79 codes supersede Part H:–L: codes. An O, S, N, or halogen atom bonded to one or more Z atoms is only coded in H:–L: if that atom is additionally bonded to U, C=U, C#N or halogen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: -Z-N=C- is coded both B731 and L355; acetals/ketals (and sulfur analogues) bonded to Z atoms are coded as acetals rather than ethers. For specific functional groups (e.g., Z-C(=T)-OH) use B791 rules and note historical date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z-halogen and specific-halogen coding (B75: and C0: interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Z atoms bonded to halogens are indexed in Subset B75:; from 1978 forward the specific halogen bonded to the Z atom is identified by a halogen code from Set C0:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dating searches across 1978 changes, include the halogen-specific C0: codes where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Z-bound carboxylic amide groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Z atom is bonded to a carboxylic amide, the Z atom is ignored and the amide is searched according to the other groups linked to it; if the amide is bonded to three Z atoms, the amide is searched in Set J3: as if Z atoms were replaced by carbon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amide fragment Z-C(=O)-NH2 is searched as an aliphatic amide; follow these substitutions when coding amide-containing fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: B7: bond-counting conventions for Z atoms
rubrics_metrics.description: In Set B7:, the number of each type of bond (e.g., Z–N, Z–C, Z–O, Z–S, Z–halogen) is totalled for all Z atoms present in the compound, ion, or ligand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acids are coded in non-ionized form (so HBF4 and H2SiF6 are coded B760); metal salts are coded ionized so B770 does not apply to NaBF4 or Na2SiF6. B770 is used for metal phosphides and Z atoms coordinated in a neutral molecule to a metal (e.g. (Ph3P)3Pt).

rubrics_metrics.name: B70–B72: Z=O, Z–O, Z–S bond-count categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets B70, B71, and B72 enumerate counts of Z=O/Z=S (B70), Z–O/Z–S (B71), and Z–S/Z=S (B72) bonds, with subcodes for one, two, three-or-more, or none as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note B720 is only searched if there is a Z atom present; B72: codes were not used for natural products (subs M1) before 1981—apply date caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valency coding for Z atoms (B8:)
rubrics_metrics.description: Valency of Z atoms is coded (e.g., B803 trivalent, B805 pentavalent, B809 other valency for boron; analogous codes exist for P and As), using the same bond-counting valency definition (double/coordination/triple counting as multiple bonds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding valency use bond-count rules; some valency codes have date applicability. Example: to ensure recall of all P+ bonded to H, search (B813 OR B814) rather than B814 alone because of historical coding differences.
